punchline: Failing without trying feels safer than failing at your best, so we wait.
thirty_sec: Psychologist Neil Fiore spent years with chronic procrastinators, many of them grad students stuck on dissertations. He found most weren't lazy at all. They believed their worth equaled their performance, so every task felt like a ruling on who they were. Delay kept the ruling away: 'I didn't really try' stings less than 'my best wasn't good enough.' The catch is that the fear never gets faced, so it hides behind 'no time' and keeps coming back.
question: What are you putting off right now, and whose judgment are you picturing when you think about finishing it?
